newsitem.title: USA: GM IN TALKS WITH SOUTH AFRICA'S DELTA.
newsitem.headline: GM IN TALKS WITH SOUTH AFRICA'S DELTA.

text.p: General Motors Corp.appeared to be edging closer to a possible return to South Africa Thursday after the company it once owned there said it was in talks with GM to increase cooperation.
Delta Motor Corp., made up of operations that GM sold in 1986 amid controversy over apartheid, said Thursday that discussions with GM were continuing.

"As a result of the changed political circumstances in South Africa, and in pursuit of its global business strategy, GM has approached Delta to discuss the potential for increased cooperation in the mutual interests of the parties," Delta said in a statement.
Delta, which produces cars originally designed by GM's Adam Opel AG unit in Germany, gave no further details on the talks.
GM and Delta in 1995 formed a joint venture in Port Elizabeth, South Africa, to make leather seat covers for export to Opel in Europe.
GM's Delphi Packard Electric unit also owns a 50.1 percent interest in South Africa's largest vehicle wiring harness maker, Auto Cable Industries Pty. Ltd.

GM spokesman Christopher Mattingley declined to comment on Delta's statement, or on GM's future plans in South Africa, but said, "We view the South African market as an important potential market for the future."
He said GM has a good relationship with Delta and noted that, as the world's largest automaker, GM is "often in discussion with a lot of partners for potential business."
Mattingley said GM was increasing its business presence in other southern African countries, including Botswana and Namibia.
But rival Ford Motor Co. has been back in South Africa since November 1994, when it acquired a 45 percent interest in South African Motor Corp., the assembly operation it divested in 1988.
Chrysler Corp. began selling export vehicles in South Africa in the fall of 1996, ending a decade-long absence.
Mattingley said GM left for business reasons, not political reasons. "I'm sure any decision to re-enter a market of that type would also be based on business reasons," he said.
GM is currently in the midst of the largest global capacity expansion in its history and is building assembly plants in Poland, Argentina, Thailand and China.
